    <title>Early Prediction of Epilepsy Seizures VLSI BCI System</title>
    <updated>2019-06-07T04:45:19Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02894v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.02894v1" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>Controlling the surrounding world and predicting future events has always seemed like a dream, but that could become a reality using a Brain-Computer/Machine Interface (BCI/BMI). Epilepsy is a group of neurological diseases characterized by epileptic seizures. It affects millions of people worldwide, with 80 percent of cases occurring in developing countries. This can result in accidents and sudden, unexpected death. Seizures can happen undetectably in newborns, comatose, or motor-impaired patients, especially due to the fact that many medical personnel is not qualified for EEG signal analysis. Therefore, a portable automated detection and monitoring solution is in high demand.
